meta.title: belgica explorer
meta.description: Every Belgian court, judicial canton, municipality and postal code, and the legal interest rates: a site built from the belgica package.

footer.builtFrom: Every page is built from <npm>belgica</npm> at build time: <docs>documentation</docs> · <source>this site's source</source>
footer.disclaimer: Reference data, not legal advice: check the official sources before relying on it. Municipality and postal-code data © Statbel, canton boundaries © NGI, CC BY 4.0.

home.title: Which court has jurisdiction where?
home.lede: Enter a postal code or a municipality to find its justice of the peace, police court and every other court with their registries' contacts. Or browse the courts, the canton map and the interest rates, all read from the package's data.
home.featureAddress: From a postal code to its municipalities, their cantons and every court with jurisdiction there. Split cities list each canton with the legal text of its area.
home.featureMap: The NGI's boundary of every canton, to find the canton of a point and draw it. Every canton has its legal basis and its municipalities.
home.featureInterest: The legal and commercial rates since 1970, with the rule for contracts from before 16 March 2013. The calculator loads only belgica/interest-rates.
home.featureCourts: Names as each court publishes them, addresses, phone numbers in national form, IBANs, opening hours and ECLI codes. Switch NL · FR · DE at the top.

interest.title: Interest calculator
interest.lede: Simple interest at the legal rate or the rate for commercial transactions, split over the rate periods it crosses: days × principal × rate ÷ 365. The calculator runs in your browser on belgica/interest-rates alone, without the court or territory data.
interest.newerContract: Contract concluded on or after 16 March 2013
interest.ambiguous: Is the separator in {amount} for thousands or for decimals? Write the amount without one (10000) or with decimals (10000,00).
interest.invalid: Enter a positive amount and a start date before the end date.
interest.missing: Part of the period has no rate on file (rates are known up to {date}); it isn't counted.
interest.disclaimer: A calculation aid, not legal advice: a judgment or contract can set other rules, such as capitalised interest.

address.title: Address lookup
address.lede: Type a street address and get its judicial canton and every court for it. In a city split over several cantons the house number decides, which a postal code can’t tell.
address.label: Address
address.placeholder: Street and number, postal code and municipality
address.none: No address found. Check the spelling, write the street name in full and give the postal code.
address.streetOnly: The register knows the street but not this house number: the point is somewhere on the street, which may itself be the boundary between two cantons. Check the number.
address.outside: This point lies in no canton: is it in Belgium?
address.onLine: The address lies on the boundary between {cantons}: the courts of each are listed, and the law decides. Read each canton’s area below.
address.near: The address is {metres} m from the boundary with {other}. The NGI drew the boundary from the law, and the law decides: read both cantons’ areas below.
address.split: <name></name> is split over several cantons; the address decides which.
address.legalText: The cantons’ areas, as the law describes them
address.source: Address from {register}. Reference data, not legal advice.
address.how: Your browser sends the address to its region’s own register: the Adressenregister in Flanders, UrbIS in Brussels, ICAR in Wallonia. For a house number the register knows, the point is on the building, so the even and odd sides of a boundary street fall in the right canton. The point is then looked up in the NGI’s canton boundaries, as findCantonsAt does, and the canton gives its courts, as getCourtsForCanton does. Within 25 m of another canton the lookup warns and shows the law’s text for both.
address.disclaimer: The canton boundaries are the NGI’s drawing of the Judicial Code’s annex: where they differ, the law decides. Reference data, not legal advice.

finder.title: Which court has jurisdiction?
finder.lede: Pick a municipality or postal code and see every court for it, from the justice of the peace to the court of appeal, with what each one hears and how to reach its registry. Where a city is split over cantons, the street address decides.
finder.loadError: The data couldn’t be loaded. Check your connection and reload the page.

finder.intro: Every Belgian municipality falls under a justice of the peace, a police court, a court of first instance and so on. In the big cities the street decides which justice of the peace, and sometimes the house number does.
finder.summary: {cantons, plural, one {Postal codes {codes} · one canton} other {Postal codes {codes} · # cantons}}
finder.split: {name} is split over {count} cantons: the street address decides which justice of the peace has jurisdiction. Enter the street and house number.
finder.outside: This address is in none of {name}’s cantons. Check the postal code, or pick the municipality it’s in.

finder.byLanguage: A Dutch- and a French-speaking court: the language of the proceedings decides.
finder.policeZoneAbout: Not a court: the local police, for a complaint or a report
finder.divisionNote: The court as a whole: which of its divisions hears a case is set by royal decree.
finder.dataNote: From the belgica package, as it was on {date}.
finder.how: The site writes each municipality’s cantons, the courts whose area holds each canton and their registries’ contacts from the package at build time, as findCourtsWithJurisdiction gives them. For a municipality split over cantons, your browser sends the street address to its region’s own register (the Adressenregister in Flanders, UrbIS in Brussels, ICAR in Wallonia) and looks the point up in the NGI’s canton boundaries, as findCantonsAt does. The link in the address bar holds the municipality and the address, so a result can be shared.
finder.mapHint: Or click the map where the address is: the point is placed in the cantons the same way.
finder.alsoCovers: Canton {canton} also covers {others}. If the point lies there, pick that municipality: the courts are the same, the police zone may not be.
